title.rendered: I Am the Bread of Life: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Jesus said, “I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger.” A morning devotional on the deepest hunger of the human soul and the only Bread that satisfies.

content.rendered:
The morning after Jesus fed five thousand people on a hillside, the crowd came looking for another meal. Jesus offered them something more. Something the manna in the wilderness could never do. Something no earthly bread has ever done. Himself.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, August 21, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And Jesus said to them, ‘I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.'”
John 6:35 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

For forty years in the wilderness, the manna appeared every morning like the dew. Small, white flakes on the ground before sunrise. Each family gathered only what they needed for that day, no more, no less. The bread from heaven kept two million people alive as they walked toward the promised land. But there was something the manna could not do. It could not satisfy the deeper hunger. The fathers ate the manna, and they still died. Something more than physical bread was needed to answer the deeper hunger of the human soul.

Fifteen hundred years later, on a hillside in Galilee, Jesus fed five thousand men plus women and children with five barley loaves and two small fish. The crowd was ecstatic. Here at last, they thought, was a new Moses, a new manna-giver. They wanted to make Him king. Jesus quietly withdrew across the sea. When the crowd found Him the next day, they came asking for more bread. They had missed the sign entirely. And that is when Jesus said the sentence they were not expecting. “I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.”

He was not offering to make more loaves. He was claiming to be the bread. The Greek phrase Jesus uses is ego eimi, the same two words spoken from the burning bush when God revealed His name to Moses. I AM. Jesus takes the divine name and joins it to the most ordinary substance on the human table. I am the bread. Not just a giver of bread. Not just a maker of bread. The bread itself. The bread of life.

The Passion Translation opens up the invitation: “Jesus replied, ‘I am the Bread of Life. Come every day to me and you will never be hungry. Believe in me and you will never be thirsty'” (John 6:35 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I am the Bread of Life. He who comes to Me will never be hungry, and he who believes in and cleaves to and trusts in and relies on Me will never thirst any more (at any time)” (John 6:35 AMPC). Cleaves to. Trusts in. Relies on. The bread is received not by baking but by believing.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, the invitation still stands. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there is a hunger inside you that no earthly bread will satisfy. The best career, the best relationship, the best success, the best experience, will still leave the deeper hunger in place. Jesus offers Himself as the answer to that hunger. He is the bread of life. Come to Him today. Believe in Him today. The hunger that has followed you for years does not have to follow you any longer. The Bread of Life is here.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the only One who satisfies the deeper hunger of my soul. I have tried other breads. Some have kept me alive but none of them have satisfied me. Today I come to Him. Today I believe in Him. Today I feed on His Word, His grace, His finished work at the cross. I refuse to try to satisfy myself with what I know will not last. The Bread of Life is enough. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is the Bread of Life. I feed on Him today. The deeper hunger of my soul is satisfied in Him. I refuse the counterfeit breads that leave me still hungry.
